title: malloc usage

steps.title: Include stdio.h header
steps.explanation:
Header for using `printf`.

This lesson covers the malloc safety pattern (allocate-check-use-free).

steps.title: Include stdlib.h header
steps.explanation:
Header for using `malloc` and `free`.

Dynamic memory-related function declarations go here.

steps.title: main function definition
steps.explanation:
The main frame is created.

In subsequent steps, we follow the standard usage order of heap memory.

steps.title: Heap memory allocation request
steps.explanation:
Request the size of one integer from the heap with `malloc(sizeof(int))`.

Returns address on success, `NULL` on failure.

steps.title: Memory allocation failure check
steps.explanation:
First check whether `p == NULL`.

NULL checking is a basic failsafe to prevent crashes.

steps.title: Output failure message
steps.explanation: Notifies the user of an allocation failure situation.

steps.title: return error code
steps.explanation:
Abnormal termination is specified with `return 1;`.

It is important not to move on after failure.

steps.title: Store value in heap memory
steps.explanation: Store the value in the heap space allocated with `*p = 100;`.

steps.title: Heap memory value output
steps.explanation: Reads `*p` and outputs the stored value.

steps.title: free heap memory
steps.explanation:
Frees the heap memory used with `free(p)`.

Pointer reuse should be avoided after freeing.

steps.title: Program successful completion
steps.explanation:
It ends normally with `return 0;`.

Summary: Using malloc always includes NULL checking and freeing.

quiz.question:
The return type of malloc is `void*`.
What does it mean?
options: It is an address without a type (undetermined).
quiz.explanation:
`void*` is ‘an address of unknown type’.
So, it is standard to use it by casting like `(int*)`.

misconceptions.wrong: Memory acquired by malloc is initialized to 0.
misconceptions.why:
If you need memory initialized to 0, you should use `calloc`.
`malloc` does not initialize for speed.

keyTakeaway: Borrow with `malloc(sizeof(type))`, check for `NULL`, and write as a pointer.
